title: Shadow export validation harness for Stripe/NetSuite invoice consistency
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We continue to see intermittent invoice mismatches and late adjustments caused by subtle deltas between the usage ledger, the export pipeline, and downstream accounting systems (Stripe/NetSuite). Root causes include retry storms, non-idempotent export lines, inconsistent timestamp bucketing, and late-arriving rate-limit credit events. Current reconciler jobs detect some anomalies after export, but they are noisy and slow to surface actionable differences to billing ops.

Goal: Build a read-only 'shadow export validation harness' that runs in parallel with the live export pipeline. The harness will compute an independent export signature and ledger snapshot for each hourly window and assert parity with the live export before downstream ingestion. Where parity fails, the harness will produce detailed diff artifacts, an anomaly ticket, and a drilldown link to a reconciliation dashboard. This will reduce the time-to-detect true export inconsistencies and provide structured evidence for automated corrective playbooks and slower corrective backfills.

Non-goals: The shadow harness is NOT intended to replace the live export or introduce extra latency into the production export path. It must be opt-in at first and run asynchronously in an isolated read-only mode. Fixes to live exports will continue to be rolled out via normal release processes.

Scope: Hourly export windows for all metered events (usage, rate-limit credits, burst credits) for customers with reserved capacity and hosted plans. Initial rollout covers US regions and single-currency invoices. Later phases will add multi-currency reconciliation, NetSuite mapping verification, and scheduled backfill workflows for late usage.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow harness runs on the same input stream as production exports but writes no changes to downstream systems (read-only).
For each export window the harness produces: (a) deterministic export signature, (b) stable per-customer delta file, and (c) a human-readable diff with the live export.
Anomaly tickets are auto-created when checksum mismatch rate > 0.1% for a 24h rolling window. Tickets must include links to the diff artifact and the reconciliation dashboard.
Export signature algorithm documented and tested (unit + integration) — signatures are collision-resistant for our event volumes.
Reconciliation dashboard surfaces reconciliation_mismatch_rate, export_checksum_pass_rate, top-10 customers by delta amount, and average time-to-detect.
Runbook item created with triage steps, severity levels, and coordinated backfill instructions.
implementation_notes: Design: append an export-signature generator to the export pipeline that mirrors production transformations but remains sidecar. The generator computes: per-customer ordered seq checksum, hourly totals, and a signed manifest (epoch, seq_start, seq_end, checksum).
Storage: diff artifacts and manifests go to a read-only S3 bucket with lifecycle 90d and are indexed in Dynamo for quick lookup by invoice_id and export_window.
Idempotency: harness must replay identical inputs and produce stable manifests — introduce an epoch-based seqnum to ensure stable ordering across retries. Avoid relying on consumer offsets alone.

Backfill: implement a 'replay-only' mode which will run the harness against historical hour windows to baseline historical mismatch rates and to seed anomaly tickets for windows that previously had silent discrepancies.
Ops: add metrics (reconciliation_mismatch_rate, export_checksum_pass_rate, mismatch_amount_total) to the billing console and create alerting thresholds.
Privacy: artifact storage must redact tokenized PII and use customer_id instead of email. Follow KMS encryption standards used by existing exports.
comments: 2025-02-12 Asha Patel: Initial triage — flagged as P0 due to growing rate of invoice adjustments reported by finance. Proposed shadow harness to provide earlier, richer evidence for fixes.
2025-02-15 Marcus Li: Architecture sketch added to Confluence (link below). Need infra review for additional storage and indexing costs. Tentative plan to run in parallel for 2 weeks in opt-in mode.

2025-02-19 Infra review (by Priya Kumar): Kafka schema extension required for stable seqnum propagation. Also recommend sampling mode first to validate perf impact. Estimated infra cost < $1.5k/mo for artifacts storage at pilot scale.
2025-02-22 PM review (Lena González): Acceptance criteria updated to include automated ticket creation and dashboard requirements. Prioritize Stripe-line parity first.

2025-02-25 Marcus Li: Implemented unit tests for signature generator; integration tests mocked Stripe export pipeline. Found edge case where retried usage events with identical timestamps produce non-deterministic ordering; added stable-sort by (timestamp, event_id).

2025-03-01 Finance (Rajiv Menon): Requested that harness also produce 'invoice_delta_report' for any customer with delta > $5 in a single window to be used by revenue ops. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-03-02 Asha Patel: Began canary run in opt-in mode for 10% of customers in US region. Early results show export_checksum_pass_rate 99.92% and three significant deltas identified (two due to delayed rate-limit credit backfills, one due to timezone bucketing disagreement).
runbook: Severity 1: mismatch_amount_total > $10k in a 1h window — page on-call, open critical incident, pause downstream ingestion for affected accounts.
Severity 2: >1% of customers with delta > $50 over 24h — create investigation ticket and assign to billing-engineering.
Triage steps: attach diff artifact, check export_checksum_pass_rate, confirm idempotency token presence, check Kafka seqnum propagation.
Backfill procedure: run replay-only backfill for affected windows, generate corrective export patch files, and schedule safe re-ingestion into billing pipeline under process lock.
